added_models.model: Population PK / exposure-response model of lenvatinib in HCC (phase 1 pool + Study 202) choosing weight-based starting dose

dose.note: Eisai's popPK/exposure-response model (healthy-volunteer, solid-tumour and Study 202 HCC data) picked 12 mg (>=60 kg) / 8 mg (<60 kg) for phase 3; no patient test yet.
dose.short: PK model picks weight-based phase 3 dose
dose.quote: We therefore recommend 12-mg and 8-mg starting doses for subjects ≥60 kg and <60 kg, respectively, in subjects with HCC Child-Pugh class A.
dose.confidence_note: Proxy opening: the analysis was published 2017 (epub 2017-05-31) but the regimen it recommends was REFLECT's from its March 2013 start (NCT01761266, bodyweight stratification), so the model existed by 2013. Full text read (PMC5575539). model_filed true on the 2018 HCC label (section 2.4 weight-based dose); the 2018 sNDA review PDFs themselves returned 404.
dose.judgement: Opening entry at first use. Model is in silico (logistic exposure-response on cycle-1 dose modifications; AUC cutoff 2430 ng·h/mL, body-weight cutoff 57.8 kg), not an animal.

dose.note: REFLECT dosed exactly the model's regimen (12 mg >=60 kg / 8 mg <60 kg) and met its OS non-inferiority primary endpoint: regimen reached and enough.
dose.short: Model's weight-based dose used; REFLECT worked
dose.quote: to receive oral lenvatinib (12 mg/day for bodyweight ≥60 kg or 8 mg/day for bodyweight <60 kg) or sorafenib 400 mg twice-daily in 28-day cycles.
dose.confidence_note: Paired by me (Tamai 2017 model vs Kudo 2018 trial); REFLECT's observed exposure by weight group is not reported in the abstract, so magnitude is null. Abstract-level reading of Kudo 2018. The 2018 FDA label (206947s007, sections 2.4 and 14.3) carries the same regimen at tier 2 but does not state the comparison.
dose.judgement: Scored same under 'reached, drug worked': the trial gave the model-chosen regimen and OS was non-inferior (HR 0.92). margin_stated true because the model named a tolerated exposure ceiling (AUC 2430 ng·h/mL, early dose modification) and set the regimen below it; patients were dosed to that target and the trial succeeded. Year is the Lancet publication (2018), not the 2017 Tamai paper, since the trial result is the patient side. No regulator review of the 2018 HCC sNDA was retrievable, so comparison_stated stays false.

added_models.model: Mouse HCC with diverse genetic drivers (hydrodynamic transposon delivery) screened for lenvatinib vs sorafenib susceptibility

efficacy.note: Driver-gene screen in a multi-driver mouse HCC model: lenvatinib eliminated FGF19-expressing tumours, sorafenib MET- and NRAS-driven ones; a patient-selection prediction before any patient test.
efficacy.short: Mouse screen: FGF19 tumours are lenvatinib-sensitive
efficacy.quote: We found that lenvatinib selectively eliminated FGF19-expressing tumors, whereas sorafenib eliminated MET- and NRAS-expressing tumors.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (paywalled); the delivery method is inferred from the paper's cited methods (Sleeping Beauty transposon, hydrodynamic injection), not read in the Methods. Same-paper opening at first use.
efficacy.judgement: A distinct system from the draft's xenograft track: a genetically engineered mouse with many driver genotypes side by side, used to choose which patients respond (prediction_level patient). Matsuki 2018's Hep3B2.1-7 FGF19 xenograft belongs to the existing xenograft track and is not duplicated here.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: model: selective elimination of FGF19-expressing tumours; patients: longer survival on lenvatinib than sorafenib in serum ST6GAL1-high (FGF19 proxy) HCC
efficacy.population: Serum ST6GAL1-high (FGF19-driven) HCC on TKI therapy
efficacy.note: Same paper: serum ST6GAL1 (an FGF19-regulated secreted protein) tracked tumour FGF19, and ST6GAL1-high patients lived longer on lenvatinib than on sorafenib.
efficacy.short: ST6GAL1-high patients do better on lenvatinib
efficacy.quote: Among patients with serum ST6GAL1-high HCC who underwent TKI therapy, lenvatinib therapy showed significantly better survival than sorafenib.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (paywalled): the patient cohort is retrospective, its size and hazard ratio were not seen, and the biomarker is a serum proxy for tumour FGF19 rather than FGF19 itself. Serum FGF19 studies point the other way (Shigesawa 2020 JGH Open: high baseline serum FGF19 plus ANG2 predicted poor lenvatinib response; Finn 2021 REFLECT: baseline serum FGF19 not predictive), but serum FGF19 is largely ileal, not tumour, so they are not scored against this track.
efficacy.judgement: Scored same at patient level: the model named the responder genotype and the same paper's patients agreed in direction. Not a retrodiction: FGF19 as a lenvatinib-selection marker was not an established clinical result before this screen. Not a trial primary endpoint (retrospective OS), so endpoint_role is null. One drug's agreement only; no prospective trial has tested it.

added_models.model: Patient-derived primary liver cancer organoids / organoid biobanks (ex vivo drug sensitivity)

efficacy.note: First member-drug use found: 52 PLC organoids from 153 patients tested on lenvatinib; resistant in vitro yet sensitive as organoid xenografts, and no patient comparison.
efficacy.short: Organoids resist lenvatinib in vitro; no patient test
efficacy.quote: PLC organoids were mostly resistant to lenvatinib in vitro but sensitive to lenvatinib in ODX models.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Earlier liver-cancer organoid papers (Broutier 2017, Nuciforo 2018) tested sorafenib only, outside the member list, so the track opens here; an earlier member-drug organoid screen may exist.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry. The in-vitro/in-vivo split is itself a warning that a dish cannot read an anti-angiogenic drug; recorded as untested, not contra, because no patient was compared.

efficacy.note: 399-organoid biobank (144 patients) screened on seven drugs incl. lenvatinib; abstract claims agreement with patient response, but which drug was compared could not be read.
efficacy.short: Biobank claims patient-response match; drug unread
efficacy.quote: we establish a PLC biobank, consisting of 399 tumor organoids derived from 144 patients, which recapitulates histopathology and genomic landscape of parental tumors, and is reliable for drug sensitivity screening, as evidenced by both in vivo models and patient response.
efficacy.confidence_note: Paywalled; full text not retrievable (Cell Press blocked two scrape attempts, no PMC copy). The abstract does not name the drug(s) in the patient-response comparison, so under the no-widening rule no status is assigned until a member drug (lenvatinib is among the seven) is confirmed. LICOB (Ji 2023, doi:10.1126/scitranslmed.adg3358, PMC10949980 full text) validated lenvatinib combinations in organoids and PDX only, not against patients.
efficacy.judgement: Kept untested with strengthens: the comparison exists in the source but cannot be attributed to a class member from what I could read; a checker with the full text can turn this into same or contra for lenvatinib.
efficacy.reason: Patient comparison claimed; member drug unverified

considered_not_added: Tai 2014 regorafenib PLC5 xenograft (doi:10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-14-0725): same system as the draft's hcc-human-xenograft-immunodeficient-mouse track; a gap on an existing track, not a missing model system

Matsuki 2018 Hep3B2.1-7 FGF19 xenograft and Finn 2021 REFLECT FGF19/FGF23 PD rise (engagement, downstream): both sit on the existing xenograft track; Finn 2021 full text even states the comparison ('Results of this analysis were consistent with the antitumor activity of lenvatinib observed in HCC xenograft models'), so that track's engagement/efficacy cells could gain a comparison_stated entry, but it is not a new system

Patient-derived xenograft co-clinical use (LICOB lenvatinib-resistant-patient PDX, Ji 2023): PDX is already inside the draft's xenograft track; no organoid-vs-patient or PDX-vs-patient lenvatinib outcome comparison found
Patient-derived organotypic tumour spheroids (JITC 2026, doi:10.1136/jitc-2025-014555): HCC PDOTS predict PD-1 blockade response against PDX, not patients, and not for a class member

Serum FGF19 / ANG2 baseline and early-change biomarkers (Shigesawa 2020 JGH Open; Chuma 2020 Cancers): patient-side readouts with no model side of their own; cited in the Myojin track's confidence note
Zebrafish or chick CAM patient-derived xenografts with lenvatinib/regorafenib: no HCC paper with a patient comparison found
Human genetic or human challenge models: none exist for VEGFR multikinase inhibition in HCC

In-silico dose models for regorafenib, donafenib, catequentinib/anlotinib: regorafenib's 160 mg came from a phase 1 MTD and no model-based dose choice with a patient comparison was found; donafenib and anlotinib have no HCC model comparison in PubMed/Europe PMC (abstract level)
Chinese real-world lenvatinib popPK (J Clin Pharmacol 2022, doi:10.1002/jcph.2103): a post-hoc PK description, no prospective prediction compared with patients
